literal: of whatever measure they are - even if - what - will become - even millet-measure - he who considers not - another man's - house/wife - entering
translation: What does it matter how great a man is? Entering another man's house without the slightest thought renders his greatness worthless.
modern: ஒருவர் எவ்வளவு பெருமை உடையவராக இருந்தாலும் என்ன பயன்? தினையளவு கூட விளைவுகளை ஆராயாமல் பிறனுடைய மனைவியிடம் செல்வது அந்தப் பெருமையை அழித்துவிடும்.
explanation: The couplet questions the value of any greatness a person might possess if they commit the grave error of desiring another man's wife. The word 'எனைத்துணையர்' (of whatever measure) emphasizes that no amount of wealth, power, or learning can compensate for this moral failure. 'தினைத்துணையும் தேரான்' (not considering even a millet's measure) vividly illustrates the complete lack of forethought and moral judgment. Entering another's house ('பிறனில் புகல்') without the slightest reflection renders all other achievements meaningless.
